Marketing Strategy01

Five things must work together.

Robotic novelty creates the first look. The strategy must turn that attention into a distinctive brand, an ownable experience and repeat behaviour.

01

Product Angle

Lead with visible robotics and theatre.

02

Brand Memory

Give the novelty an easy name and recognisable face.

03

Distinctive World

Use Japanese-inspired character energy and weirdness.

04

Theatre

Create a reveal a normal café cannot copy.

05

Built-in Marketing

Let cups, foam and sharing drive the next order.

Novelty/Memory/Distinctiveness/Experience/Repeat
01 / Product Angle02

Lead with the robotic novelty.

A six-axis arm behind glass is already more interesting than another café counter. The machine should perform, reveal and invite attention.

01

Technology in full view

The arm is the show — not something to hide.

02

A visible ritual

Order, movement, dispense and collection create theatre.

03

A story worth sharing

People film what normal coffee keeps behind the counter.

02 / Brand Memory03

Brand the novelty. Make it memorable.

Technology creates a first look. A distinctive brand creates recognition, recall and repeat behaviour.

01 · Name

Short & sayable

Short, easy to say and easy to ask for.

02 · Character

One memorable face

One memorable face aligned with the robot.

03 · Colour

Pink & black

Pink and black create instant recognition.

04 · Voice

Cute & strange

Cute, strange and slightly rebellious.

The machine gets attention.→The brand earns memory.
03 / Distinctive World04

Japanese-inspired weirdness creates a world.

Borrow the energy of vending, gacha and character culture — not a costume or a claim to be Japanese.

01

Vending theatre

Technology stays visible and enjoyable.

02

Character culture

A mascot carries emotion across every touchpoint.

03

Gacha anticipation

Collectable surprise: you don’t know which Moki mood you’ll get.

04

Designed weirdness

Odd copy, glitches and details make the category talkable.

日本風のエネルギー/Japanese-inspired energy
04 / Experience05

Do not compete with baristas.
Build what they cannot.

A robotic kiosk should not imitate a coffee shop. It should turn speed, precision and automation into theatre.

Watch→Reveal→Share
Normal cafés own hospitality.
Moki owns novelty.
The goal is not to replace a barista. It is to create a coffee people want to show someone.
05 / Built-in Marketing06

Make every order advertise the next.

The cup and foam turn product cost into owned media: a reveal people compare, photograph and carry away.

01

Order

A familiar coffee choice.

02

Reveal

A mood appears on cup and foam.

03

Compare

People show each other what they got.

04

Share

The mood becomes social shorthand.

05

Return

Rare and seasonal drops create another reason.

Designed into the product margin/Carried out of the machine
The Current Brand07

Clever machine. Forgettable brand.

The hardware creates theatre. The brand does not yet give people an easy name, character, visual code or repeatable ritual to remember.

01

Name friction

Harder to pronounce, spell and request.

02

No character asset

The robot performs without a personality people can follow.

03

Limited product memory

Cup, foam and digital do not yet create a repeatable loop.

The Moki Answer08

MOKI makes the machine memorable.

A short name, robot-aligned character, electric colour and expressive system make the novelty easy to recognise and repeat.

01

Easy name

MOKI is short, phonetic and requestable.

02

Memorable character

Cute, fun and robotic — the face matches the product.

03

One connected world

Machine, cups, foam, packaging and website reinforce each other.

The Name09

A good consumer brand becomes the thing people ask for.

“Let’s get a Moki.”
is easier than
“Let’s get an Ahstae.”
MOKI is short, easy to say and connected to the character./Lead domain: moki.coffee
